summary: Michiko Yusa specializes in religious studies, philosophy, and Japanology. She completed doctoral studies under Raimon Panikkar (~1978–1983) and became a professor in the Department of Foreign Languages at Western Washington University around 1986.
Michio Kamikawa works in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Ritsumeikan University and held a post at Aichi Prefectural University around 1999.

Michio Yano is an Indologist and historian. He studied at Kyoto University, including under Kiyoshi Yabuuchi (~1967–1972), and at Brown University under David Pingree (~1974–1976). From 1973 to 2015, he was a professor at Kyoto Sangyo University.
Michitaro Tanaka was a philosopher who studied at Kyoto University under Hidenaka Tanaka (~1923–1926). He held posts at Ryukoku University (~1940–1947) and Tokyo University of Education (~1947–1950).

Michitoshi Baraida works in Buddhist studies and Indology, having studied under Jien Abe and J. R. Joshi. He has held positions at Otani University, Toho Kenkyukai, Toho Gakuin, and the Nakamura Hajime Eastern Institute.
Michiya Ito pursued graduate studies at Tohoku University (attested 1986–1990) and later held a post there (attested 2001–2004).
Michiyo Hoshi is a specialist in Tibetology and linguistics. She has held research posts at the Research Institute for Languages and Cultures of Asia and Africa and at the Toyo Bunko (attested 2003).
Midori Nishino specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. She completed doctoral coursework at Taisho University (attested 2006) and subsequently worked there as a researcher (attested 2010–2015).

Migmar Tsering was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar who studied under Khenpo Appey Rinpoche. He held posts at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies, the Tibetan Academy of Social Sciences, and served as head of Sakya College.

Mihai Șora was a philosopher who studied under Mircea Eliade at the University of Bucharest (~1934–1938), later studying at the University of Paris and CNRS. He worked at the State Publishing House for Literature and Arts (~1959–1969).

Mikaël Bauer specializes in Buddhist studies and Japanology. He studied at Kanazawa University under Noritoshi Aramaki and Paul Hoornaert, and earned his PhD at Harvard under Ryuichi Abe. He is Associate Professor of Japanese Religions at McGill University.
Mike Kestemont works in computational linguistics. He served as a postdoctoral fellow at the Research Foundation - Flanders (~2012–2015) and has held posts at the University of Antwerp (~2013, 2025).

Mikel Burley works in philosophy, religious studies, and Indology. He studied at Essex and Bristol under Jay M. Bernstein, Jonardon Ganeri, Brian Carr, and John Peacock, and became Associate Professor of Religion and Philosophy at the University of Leeds.
Miki Ujiie works in Buddhist studies and Indology. After studying abroad at Tribhuvan University, he served as a lecturer at Koyasan University (attested 1970).
Mikio Otsuki specializes in Buddhist studies and Japanology. By 2007, he was attested as a professor at Hanazono University and a research fellow at Manpuku-ji.

Mikisaburo Mori was a scholar of philosophy and sinology who earned degrees from Kyoto and Osaka universities. He held academic posts at Kyoto University, Osaka High School, Osaka University (professor 1966–1973), and Bukkyo University (~1973–1982).
Milman Parry was a linguist who studied at UC Berkeley and the University of Paris under Antoine Meillet. He held a post at Harvard University from around 1929 until 1935.
Milton Singer was an Indologist who studied at the University of Texas at Austin and the University of Chicago. He held a faculty post at the University of Chicago from around 1940 to 1979.
Min Ling Khenchen Tsewang Rigdzin studied under Dudjom Rinpoche and Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche.
Min Thu Wun was a linguist who studied under Pe Maung Tin at the University of Rangoon (~1926–1935) before studying at the University of Oxford (~1936–1939).
